portName: Villefranche-sur-Mer (tender) and Port of Nice (Port Lympia)
seoTitle: Nice cruise port (Villefranche): tender, train and bus guide
seoDescription: Nice cruise calls 2026: most ships tender at Villefranche. TER to Nice €3.60 in about 5 min, bus 600 to Monaco €2.10 contactless. New caps on big ships.
quickAnswer: Most large ships anchor off Villefranche-sur-Mer and tender passengers to the Port de la Santé; only small ships berth in Nice's Port Lympia. From Villefranche, the TER train reaches Nice-Ville in about 5 minutes for €3.60 full fare, and bus 600 (the old line 100) runs to Nice and Monaco for €2.10 with a contactless card (2026). Be back at the tender pier 90 minutes before all-aboard, or two hours if you rely on the train.
intro: "Nice" on a cruise itinerary almost always means Villefranche-sur-Mer, a deep bay 5 km east of the city where big ships anchor and run tenders. Small ships can berth in Nice's own harbour, Port Lympia, below Castle Hill. Since a prefectoral order of 9 December 2025, the Alpes-Maritimes coast limits big-ship calls: only one ship of more than 1,300 passengers a day at each anchorage, and no more than 15 calls a month in July and August. Once ashore, Nice, Monaco and Èze are all reachable by train or bus for a few euros, so the real constraint is the tender queue, not distance.
tenderNotes: Large ships anchor in the Rade de Villefranche and tender to the Port de la Santé, the small harbour at the foot of the old town, which has a tourist information desk and toilets. Since the 2025–2026 prefectoral framework, only one ship carrying more than 1,300 passengers may call per day at Villefranche, which keeps tender piers less crowded than before. Ships under about 180 m can berth alongside in Nice at Port Lympia instead. Cannes is a separate tender port about 30 km west, covered by the same rules; this guide does not cover it.

terminals.name: Villefranche-sur-Mer tender pier (Port de la Santé)
terminals.notes: Where tenders from anchored ships land. Villefranche old town is on the doorstep. The train station is about 600 m away, roughly 10 minutes on foot with stairs and a short climb. Nice centre is about 5 km west.

terminals.name: Port of Nice (Port Lympia, Bassin Lympia)
terminals.notes: Berth for small ships, roughly under 180 m. Vieux Nice and Castle Hill are a short walk west round the harbour.

walkability.detail: Villefranche itself is fully walkable from the tender pier, but its lanes are steep and stepped. Nice is not a walk from Villefranche: take the train (about 5 minutes) or a bus. From Nice-Ville station, Vieux Nice is about 20 minutes on foot or a few stops on tram line 1. From Port Lympia, Vieux Nice is a short, flat walk.

transportSections.detail: Villefranche-sur-Mer station is about 10 minutes' walk from the tender pier, with stairs. Around 60 trains a day run between roughly 06:30 and 23:30. Buy at the station machine or in the SNCF Connect app before boarding. Trains run on to Monaco–Monte-Carlo in the other direction, about 15 minutes away.

transportSections.cost: Check the station machine or SNCF Connect
transportSections.detail: Same line as Nice, heading east. Monaco station is underground and its exits are well inside the city; allow time to find the right exit for the Rock or Monte-Carlo.

transportSections.cost: €2.10 with contactless card or phone; €2.50 cash to the driver (2026)
transportSections.time: Slower than the train; traffic on the coast road
transportSections.detail: Line 100 was renumbered 600 in April 2024. It runs along the coast road through Villefranche, Beaulieu and Èze-sur-Mer to Monaco and Menton, every 10–15 minutes on weekdays and about every 20 minutes at weekends. Tap your card on the validator. A Lignes d'Azur ticket is valid only for trips that do not enter Monaco. Buses fill up in summer; the train is more reliable on a tight schedule.

transportSections.mode: Lignes d'Azur bus 15 to Nice port
transportSections.cost: €1.70 Solo ticket on a rechargeable card (2026)
transportSections.detail: Lignes d'Azur no longer sells paper tickets; fares load onto a rechargeable card. Drivers sell a €4 card to passengers without one. The Octroi stop is about 7 minutes' walk from the tender pier.

transportSections.time: A few minutes Gare Thiers to Cathédrale–Vieille Ville
transportSections.detail: Useful from Nice-Ville station (Gare Thiers stop) to Vieux Nice. Validate each time you board.

transportSections.cost: Check the current fare on the ZOU! site or with the driver
transportSections.detail: Runs Nice Vauban – Villefranche – Col de Villefranche – Èze Village – Monaco, daily in summer, with gaps of up to two hours between some departures. Check the current timetable before relying on it for the return.

returnTiming.rule: Be at the Villefranche tender pier by 15:30 for a 17:30 all-aboard (two hours ahead if returning by train or bus).
returnTiming.detail: The train from Nice is only about 5 minutes and from Monaco about 15, but the walk from Villefranche station to the pier has stairs and takes 10 minutes, and tender queues build in the last hour. Buses on the coast road are slowed by traffic in summer.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: If you miss a train, the next one is rarely more than 20–30 minutes away in the daytime. Taxis wait at Nice-Ville station and in Monaco; agree the fare to the Villefranche tender pier before you get in. Call the port agent number printed in your daily programme if you will be late.

excursionAdvice: Nice, Villefranche and Monaco are easy and cheap by train, so most fit passengers do not need a ship tour. The ship's coach earns its price for Èze plus Monaco in one day, because the 602 bus to Èze Village runs irregularly, and for anyone who cannot manage stairs at Villefranche station. Saint-Paul-de-Vence is inland and awkward by public transport on a cruise day; a tour makes sense there.

dayPlan.intro: Assumes anchoring at 08:00 and first tenders ashore by about 08:30. Plan for Nice; swap the middle for Monaco if you prefer.

steps.what: Tender to the Port de la Santé. Walk about 10 minutes, with stairs, to Villefranche-sur-Mer station.
TER to Nice-Ville (about 5 minutes). Tram line 1 from Gare Thiers to Cathédrale–Vieille Ville.
Cours Saleya market (flowers and food; antiques on Mondays).
Free lift up Castle Hill from the Quai des États-Unis end; views over the Baie des Anges and Port Lympia from the 92 m viewpoint.
Walk down into the lanes of Vieux Nice: Place Rossetti and the cathedral, Rue Droite.
Socca and pissaladière for lunch in Vieux Nice.
Walk the Promenade des Anglais westward from the Quai des États-Unis.
Tram back to Gare Thiers; catch a TER to Villefranche by 14:45.
Chapelle Saint-Pierre on the quay (Wednesday to Sunday) or a walk round the harbour.
At the tender pier, two hours before all-aboard.

sights.name: Vieux Nice
sights.why: The old town's narrow lanes between Castle Hill and the Cours Saleya, with Baroque churches and food shops.
sights.tip: Tram line 1 to Cathédrale–Vieille Ville puts you at its northern edge.

sights.name: Castle Hill (Colline du Château)
sights.why: Park on the site of the old castle, with a viewpoint at 92 m over the Promenade des Anglais and Port Lympia, and an artificial waterfall.
sights.tip: The free lift starts near the Quai des États-Unis; the Lesage stairs are the alternative. Lift hours vary with the season.

sights.name: Cours Saleya
sights.why: Market square at the heart of Vieux Nice: flowers and produce most days, antiques and bric-à-brac on Mondays.
sights.tip: Go in the morning, before the stalls pack up.

sights.name: Promenade des Anglais
sights.why: The seafront walk along the Baie des Anges.
sights.tip: Start at the Quai des États-Unis end, by the old town, and walk west as far as time allows.

sights.name: Èze Village and the Jardin Exotique
sights.why: Hilltop medieval village between Villefranche and Monaco, with a cactus garden at the summit.
sights.cost: Garden: €4 for ages 12–17 and students; free under 12 (2026)
sights.tip: Bus 602 from Villefranche or Nice, or line 82 from Nice; check return times first. The garden opens 09:00–18:30 in October, 09:00–16:30 from November (2026). It is not wheelchair accessible.

sights.name: Monaco
sights.why: The principality is about 15 minutes by train from Villefranche: the Rock with the palace, the casino district of Monte-Carlo, and the harbour.
sights.cost: Free to walk; palace and museums charged (check official sites)
sights.tip: Lignes d'Azur tickets are not valid into Monaco on bus 600; use contactless or the train.

sights.name: Chapelle Saint-Pierre (Cocteau Chapel), Villefranche
sights.why: Small fishermen's chapel on the quay decorated by Jean Cocteau.
sights.tip: Open Wednesday to Sunday, 09:30–12:30 and 14:00–18:00; closed mid-November to mid-December. Cash or cheque only.

sights.name: Villefranche old town and Citadel
sights.why: Steep lanes and stepped streets just above the tender pier, with the 16th-century citadel at the western end of the harbour.
sights.tip: A good plan for the last hour before tenders back, since you are already beside the pier.

beaches.name: Plage des Marinières, Villefranche
beaches.howToGetThere: Walk along the shore from the tender pier towards the railway station; the beach runs below the line.
beaches.note: The town beach, sheltered by the bay and the closest swim to the tender pier.

beaches.name: Nice seafront beaches
beaches.howToGetThere: Train to Nice-Ville, then walk or tram to the Promenade des Anglais.
beaches.cost: Free public stretches; private beach clubs charge
beaches.note: Pebbles, not sand. Water shoes help.

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming the ship docks in Nice.
commonMistakes.fix: Most ships anchor at Villefranche, 5 km away. Check your daily programme for the tender pier and the train or bus from there.
The coastal Nice–Monaco–Menton line has been 600 since April 2024. Pay by contactless card for the lower fare.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using a Lignes d'Azur ticket on bus 600 into Monaco.
commonMistakes.fix: Lignes d'Azur tickets cover only trips that do not enter Monaco. Tap a contactless card instead.

commonMistakes.mistake: Forgetting that Villefranche station has stairs.
commonMistakes.fix: Allow 10 minutes from the station to the pier, more with limited mobility, and add the tender queue on top.

commonMistakes.mistake: Going to Èze Village without checking the bus back.
commonMistakes.fix: Bus 602 has gaps of up to two hours. Note the return times before you leave, or take a tour.

commonMistakes.mistake: Planning the Cocteau Chapel for a Monday or Tuesday.
commonMistakes.fix: It opens Wednesday to Sunday only. Bring cash.

safety: Nice and Villefranche are safe for daytime visitors, but pickpocketing is a known problem on the crowded coastal trains and buses, at Nice-Ville station, in Vieux Nice and on the Promenade des Anglais. Keep phones out of back pockets and bags closed on the train and bus 600. Watch for e-scooters and bikes on the Promenade. Villefranche's lanes are steep and slippery in rain.
scams: Pickpocketing on the Nice–Monaco trains and bus 600, often by people who crowd you at the doors. Keep bags in front and stand away from the doors.
Clipboard 'petition' or survey approaches on the Promenade des Anglais and in Vieux Nice, used to ask for money or distract while a partner lifts a wallet. Do not stop.
Unlicensed drivers near the Villefranche tender pier offering 'tours' or rides. Use the official taxi rank and agree the fare first.
accessibility: Tenders at Villefranche are the main barrier: wheelchair transfer depends on sea conditions and the ship's tender design, so ask the ship. The waterfront by the tender pier is flat, but the walk to Villefranche station includes stairs and the old town is stepped. In Nice, the Promenade des Anglais and the tram are step-free, and the Castle Hill lift avoids the climb. Èze's Jardin Exotique is not wheelchair accessible. Small-ship passengers docking at Port Lympia have the easiest access to Nice.
rainyDay: Vieux Nice's covered market stalls and churches, and the Cocteau Chapel in Villefranche, work in light rain. Monaco is a good wet-day choice, with large indoor attractions within reach of the station. Avoid Castle Hill and Èze in heavy rain: both involve steep, slippery paths.
crowdTips: Since the prefectoral order of 9 December 2025, only one ship over 1,300 passengers may call per day at Villefranche, July and August are limited to 15 calls a month, and disembarking passengers are capped at an average of 2,000 per call with a ceiling of 3,000. Nice's new mayor, Éric Ciotti, accepted this framework in April 2026, ending the city's attempts at its own bans, which the courts had suspended. Expect the coastal trains and bus 600 to be busy late morning and around 16:00–18:00. Vieux Nice and Monaco's old town are fullest at midday.

faqs.a: Usually, yes. Most cruise ships anchor off Villefranche-sur-Mer and tender passengers ashore. Small ships, roughly under 180 m, can berth in Nice's Port Lympia.

faqs.q: How do I get from Villefranche to Nice?
faqs.a: Walk about 10 minutes to Villefranche-sur-Mer station and take the TER to Nice-Ville: about 5 minutes and €3.60 full fare (2026). Bus 600 and Lignes d'Azur bus 15 also run to Nice.

faqs.q: How do I get from Villefranche to Monaco?
faqs.a: The train takes about 15 minutes. Bus 600 is slower but costs €2.10 with a contactless card (2026).

faqs.q: Is bus 100 still running from Nice to Monaco?
faqs.a: It was renumbered 600 in April 2024 and still runs along the coast every 10–15 minutes on weekdays.

faqs.q: Are there limits on cruise ships at Nice and Villefranche?
faqs.a: Yes. A prefectoral order of 9 December 2025 allows only one ship over 1,300 passengers per day, caps July and August at 15 calls a month, and limits disembarking passengers to an average of 2,000 per call (maximum 3,000).

faqs.q: What can I do in Nice in one day from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: Train to Nice, then Cours Saleya, Castle Hill by the free lift, Vieux Nice, socca for lunch and the Promenade des Anglais, with time for Villefranche harbour before the last tenders.
Yes, by bus 602 from Villefranche or Nice, or line 82 from Nice, but departures are irregular. Check the return times before you go.

faqs.q: Is Nice safe for cruise passengers?
faqs.a: Yes in daytime. The main risk is pickpocketing on the coastal trains and buses and in busy parts of Vieux Nice.
